patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Right leg weakness and unsteady gait

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: The patient is somnolent and slightly confused, oriented to person but not to place or time. Mild lymphadenopathy is noted.

questions: Did the right leg weakness start suddenly (within minutes to hours) or gradually (over days to weeks)?
Do you have any numbness or pain in the right leg (or any back pain that radiates down the leg)?
On exam, does the right leg show increased muscle tone or hyperreflexia (stiffness or brisk reflexes) compared with the left?
Have you had any changes in bladder or bowel control (new urinary retention/incontinence or constipation) since the weakness began?

On exam, can you tell me whether the weakness is more like trouble initiating movement (slowness/rigidity) or actual loss of strength (a specific muscle group), and does it worsen with repetitive use?
Do you have any difficulty with balance or walking that worsens with turning your head or rolling over in bed (episodes of spinning/vertigo)?
On exam, is there any numbness or loss of sensation in the right leg (and if so, does it follow a specific pattern like a stripe/dermatome or a stocking distribution)?
Have you noticed any changes in your foot position—such as “foot drop” or trouble lifting the front of your foot when walking?
Have you noticed any new back pain, or a change in balance/coordination when standing still with your eyes closed (Romberg test)?
Have you had any recent changes in your vision or speech (or numbness/weakness in your arms/face) along with the right leg symptoms?
answers: “Doctor, it started gradually over the past year, not suddenly.”
“Doctor, I don’t have numbness or significant pain in my right leg, and I haven’t noticed any back pain that radiates down the leg.”
“Doctor, I haven’t noticed any stiffness or weakness in my right leg, and I’m not aware of any change in reflexes between my legs.”
“Doctor, I haven’t had any new bladder or bowel problems—no urinary retention or incontinence, and no new constipation.”
“Doctor, I don’t have clear loss of strength in a specific part of my right leg, and I haven’t noticed any slowness or rigidity. I also haven’t noticed anything that worsens with repetitive use.”
“Doctor, I haven’t had any trouble with balance or walking, and I don’t get spinning or vertigo when turning my head or rolling over in bed.”
“Doctor, I don’t have numbness or any noticeable loss of sensation in my right leg, and I haven’t seen any specific patch or stripe-like area of reduced feeling.”
“Doctor, I haven’t noticed any foot drop or trouble lifting the front of my foot when I walk.”
“Doctor, I haven’t had any new back pain, and I don’t notice any change in balance or coordination when standing still with my eyes closed.”
“Doctor, no—I've not had any changes in my vision or speech, and I haven’t had any numbness or weakness in my arms or face either.”
